g.text: Core Evidentiary Principle of Forensic Mitochondrial DNA Testing [Amo19b, Car26b]

text.style: font-size: 7.5px; font-family: 'Arial', 'Helvetica', 'Liberation Sans', 'DejaVu Sans', sans-serif; text-anchor: start; fill: #4d4d4d

g.text: • Maternal relatives share an identical mtDNA profile; match supports lineage correspondence, NOT individualisation.

text.style: font-size: 7.5px; font-family: 'Arial', 'Helvetica', 'Liberation Sans', 'DejaVu Sans', sans-serif; text-anchor: start; fill: #4d4d4d

g.text: • Unrelated individuals in the population may also share common haplotypes by chance through shared distant ancestry.

text.style: font-size: 7.5px; font-family: 'Arial', 'Helvetica', 'Liberation Sans', 'DejaVu Sans', sans-serif; text-anchor: start; fill: #4d4d4d

g.text: • Direct nuclear autosomal comparison remains required to achieve individual-level source attribution.

text.style: font-style: italic; font-size: 7.5px; font-family: 'Arial', 'Helvetica', 'Liberation Sans', 'DejaVu Sans', sans-serif; text-anchor: end; fill: #8c8c8c
